subject: computer-science
title: Databases: Stretch — Normalisation
welcome_lead: Time to tidy data — eliminate duplication with normalisation.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science stretch adventure on database normalisation (1NF, 2NF, 3NF) intuition.
final_note: You can spot redundancy and design cleaner database tables.

concepts.def: An organised, persistent store of data.
Rows are records; columns are fields.
A field that uniquely identifies each record.
Language to query and manage a relational database.
A request to select or change data.

walkthroughs.body_html: A cell holding 'maths, english, art' breaks 1NF. Split into multiple rows or a separate table so each cell holds one value.
If Students stores ClassTeacherName, the teacher's name depends on the class, not the student. Move teacher to a Classes table — fewer updates needed if a teacher changes name.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Normalisation”?
options: A primary key made of two or more fields.
Atomic values — one fact per cell.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Redundancy”?
options: Atomic values — one fact per cell.
A primary key made of two or more fields.
Same data stored in multiple places.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “3NF”?
options: A primary key made of two or more fields.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Composite key”?
options: Same data stored in multiple places.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “1NF”?
options: Same data stored in multiple places.
Atomic values — one fact per cell.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “2NF”?
options: Same data stored in multiple places.
Atomic values — one fact per cell.
A primary key made of two or more fields.
